title: Direct and indirect object pronouns, y and en
spec: Pronouns: object: direct and indirect; use of y, en
summary: Direct object pronouns replace a noun that the verb acts on directly: le (him/it), la (her/it), les (them): Je regarde le match → Je le regarde.
le and la become l' before a vowel or silent h: J'aime cette chanson → Je l'aime.
me, te, nous, vous can be direct or indirect: Il me voit (he sees me), Il me parle (he speaks to me). me and te become m' and t' before a vowel.
Indirect object pronouns replace à + a person: lui (to him / to her), leur (to them): Je parle à ma mère → Je lui parle. leur never adds an -s here.
Common verbs with à + person: parler à, téléphoner à, dire à, demander à, donner à, offrir à, envoyer à, écrire à, répondre à.
y replaces à + a place or thing, or a place after en, dans, chez etc.: Je vais au parc → J'y vais. Je joue au foot → J'y joue.
en replaces de + noun (du, de la, de l', des): Je bois du lait → J'en bois. J'ai besoin d'argent → J'en ai besoin.
With a number or quantity, use en and keep the number or quantity at the end: J'ai deux sœurs → J'en ai deux.
In simple tenses all these pronouns go straight before the verb: Je les vois. Elle leur téléphone. Nous y allons.

cards.front: What are the direct object pronouns, and where do they go?
cards.back: me (me), te (you), le (him / it), la (her / it), nous (us), vous (you), les (them). me, te, le, la become m', t', l' before a vowel or silent h. They go straight before the verb: Je le vois. Il m'aide.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.en: I watch it in the evening.
cards.why: la télévision is feminine singular, so the direct object pronoun is la, placed before the verb.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.prompt: Nous attendons **le bus** devant le collège.
cards.en: We wait for it in front of the school.
cards.why: attendre takes a direct object (no preposition, unlike English 'wait for'), so le bus becomes le, which shortens to l' before the vowel.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.why: mes grands-parents is plural, so the pronoun is les. je no longer shortens because les starts with a consonant.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.why: l'ordinateur is masculine singular (le), and le becomes l' before the vowel of achète.

cards.prompt: Tu vois souvent ton cousin ? — Oui, je ___ vois tous les week-ends.
cards.en: Do you often see your cousin? — Yes, I see him every weekend.
cards.why: voir takes a direct object, so 'him' is le, placed before the verb.

cards.en: Your brother is looking for you everywhere!
cards.why: chercher takes a direct object, and 'you' (tu form) as an object pronoun is te, before the verb.

cards.front: What are lui and leur, and when do you use them?
cards.back: Indirect object pronouns: they replace à + a person. lui = to him or to her; leur = to them. Je parle à mon père → Je lui parle. Je téléphone à mes amis → Je leur téléphone. leur as a pronoun never takes an -s.

cards.front: Name some common verbs followed by à + person (so they take lui / leur).
cards.back: parler à, téléphoner à, dire à, demander à, donner à, offrir à, envoyer à, écrire à, répondre à, prêter à, ressembler à. Watch out: English 'I phone her' and 'I ask him' are je lui téléphone and je lui demande in French.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.prompt: Je téléphone **à ma grand-mère** le dimanche.
cards.why: téléphoner à + person takes an indirect object pronoun: à ma grand-mère → lui.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.prompt: Nous offrons un cadeau **à nos professeurs**.
cards.why: à + plural people becomes leur, which goes before the verb.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.prompt: Le prof explique la règle **aux élèves**.
answers: Le prof leur explique la règle.
cards.en: The teacher explains the rule to them.
cards.why: aux élèves = à + les élèves, plural people, so the indirect object pronoun is leur.

cards.prompt: Mes copains m'ont envoyé un message, alors je ___ ai répondu tout de suite.
cards.en: My friends sent me a message, so I replied to them straight away.
cards.why: répondre à + people takes leur, which goes before avoir in the perfect.

cards.front: What does y replace, and what does it mean?
cards.back: à + a place or thing, or a place after en, dans, chez, sur etc. It means 'there' or 'about it / to it'. Je vais au cinéma → J'y vais. Elle habite en Suisse → Elle y habite. Je pense à l'examen → J'y pense.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.prompt: Je vais **à la piscine** le mercredi.
cards.why: à + a place becomes y, before the verb; je shortens to j' before y.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.why: au Canada is a place introduced by à (au = à + le), so it becomes y.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.why: jouer à + a sport is à + a thing, so au tennis becomes y.

cards.prompt: Le Maroc ? Nous ___ allons cet été.
cards.en: Morocco? We're going there this summer.
cards.why: 'there' referring to a place already mentioned is y, placed before the verb.

cards.front: What does en replace, and what does it mean?
cards.back: de + noun, including du, de la, de l', des and verbs with de (avoir besoin de, parler de). It means 'some', 'any', 'of it' or 'of them'. Je bois du jus → J'en bois. Il a besoin d'aide → Il en a besoin. Je n'en veux pas.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun.
cards.prompt: Je mange **des fruits** tous les jours.
cards.why: des + noun is replaced by en, before the verb; je shortens to j' before en.

cards.prompt: Des frites ? Mon petit frère ___ mange tous les jours !
cards.en: Chips? My little brother eats them every day!
cards.why: The understood object is des frites (des + noun), so the pronoun is en, not les.

cards.front: How do you use en with numbers and quantities?
cards.back: Replace the noun with en and keep the number or quantity word after the verb: J'ai deux sœurs → J'en ai deux. Il y a beaucoup de touristes → Il y en a beaucoup. J'ai une voiture → J'en ai une. English often leaves 'of them' out, but French cannot leave out en.

cards.instruction: Replace the word in bold with a pronoun, keeping the number.
cards.why: With a number, the noun becomes en before the verb and the number stays at the end: j'en ai trois.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a pronoun, keeping the quantity.
cards.why: de + noun after a quantity becomes en before the verb; the quantity un kilo stays after the verb.
